function: Predictive beamforming: an all-MLP patch-mixer maps historical CSIT directly to the RSMA precoder and common-rate allocation, without a separate CSI estimation step (p. 5, p. 9).
system: Downlink MISO: one BS with a 13x13 UPA ELAA (M=169), 10 single-antenna users, 1-layer RSMA, LoS hybrid near/far-field, 3.5 GHz, no RIS (p. 3, 10, 11).
method: MLP-Mixer (all-MLP patch-mixing) predictor trained unsupervised with the geometric-mean-rate loss; distributed training by federated learning with gradient averaging at the BS (p. 8-10).
data_channel: Own simulator: LoS hybrid-field channel (far-field planar wave, near-field spherical wave), exponentially distributed user distances, CSI estimation error; 70%:30% train/test split of generated samples (p. 4, 10).
test_conditions: Same simulated setting for training and testing (70%:30% split); 13x13 antennas, 10 users, 30 dB, 40 km/h by default, one parameter varied at a time (p. 10-12).
baselines: Learned: centralized and FL-trained CNN, LSTM, Transformer predictors; SDMA transmission with the same learned predictors; no non-learned beamformer (optimization, outdated CSI) evaluated (p. 10-11).
metrics: Geometric mean of ergodic user rates (GMER), minimum ergodic user rate, ergodic sum-rate, batch processing time, and training loss versus training time (p. 11-13).
complexity: Order O(2N K T0 iota1^2) for the N-layer MLP-mixer (p. 9); measured batch processing time of milliseconds versus M and N (p. 12-13).
q1_support: p. 10: "the CSI samples are generated from the hybrid-field channel model described in Section II"; p. 4: "We consider a Line-of-Sight (LoS) path communication channel in this study". Custom simulator; no 3GPP, DeepMIMO or measured data.
q2_support: p. 10: "The entire dataset is carefully divided into training and testing sets following a 70%:30% ratio"; p. 11: "we will keep all other variables constant and modify one specific parameter within the default setting". Missing: any statement that a trained model is tested on an unseen scenario, band, or configuration.
q3_support: p. 10: "three baseline deep learning approaches: (1) CNN, (2) LSTM, and (3) Transformer". Learned baselines only; Figs. 7-14 (p. 11-13) plot only learned predictors, with SDMA also driven by them; no non-learned method is compared.
q4_support: p. 9: "the complexity of the N -layer MLP-mixer module is O{2N KT0"; p. 12: "all these approaches require mere milliseconds for generating beamformers" (Fig. 13, p. 13).
q5_support: p. 10: "the CSI samples are generated from the hybrid-field channel model described in Section II". Self-generated data; no code or data link and no public dataset or measurement is used.
notes: FL aggregates gradients digitally (uplink 100 Mbps, p. 13), only to train the beamforming predictor, so area 3 and not 7. STAR-RIS appears only as future work (p. 14). The text compares velocity degradation with results reported in survey [17] (p. 12), which is not a baseline run in the paper. The paper does not say whether the model is retrained for each swept M, N, or T0, which change its input size (p. 7-8).
